$schema-doc: devtools/coverage_decisions.json -- the CURATED half of the shared-surface spec. See devtools/header_intersection.py's header for how it is applied, and devtools/README-coverage-decisions.md for the schema. This file is HAND-WRITTEN decisions only, NOT harvested: it sits on top of the machine-generated vendor/*.json manifests and records the handful of human judgements the manifests cannot derive -- each module's contract class, and the shared names a whole-surface module deliberately does not wrap. Everything derivable stays derived in the manifests; only exceptions live here.

contract_classes.whole-surface: Promises to wrap everything the two backends share (WWR_FUNCTION spells both names). A shared name absent from the module source is a DEFECT and fails --coverage -- UNLESS it is listed under this module's `omissions`, which turns a named, justified gap into a pass.
contract_classes.curated-subset: Demand-complete: carries a wwr* name only once a consumer (a wrapper, a test, or the example) reaches for it, never the full intersection. --coverage REPORTS its `missing` list as a discovery menu and does not fail. Completeness is enforced elsewhere (the compiler, test/shared/alias_coverage.py, the dispatch tables).

omissions.why: A bf16 scalar convenience struct with implicit float conversions, referenced by no function signature -- it exists only for caller convenience, so neither cublas_v2.cppm nor hipsparse.cppm exports it. Not stubbed, simply not exported.

cuSOLVER's multi-GPU dense-solve API. Wholly deprecated in CUDA 13 (every cusolverMg* function carries CUSOLVERMG_DEPRECATED), and there is no ROCm counterpart -- no multi-GPU dense-solve API exists anywhere in rocSOLVER or hipSOLVER (issue #177, resolved). Re-exported by cusolverMg.cppm on the CUDA side with the deprecation attribute intact; no HIP twin to wrap.
cuSPARSE's Preview SpMM-with-custom-operators API has no hipSPARSE counterpart -- verified by grepping the installed hipSPARSE headers, nothing exists. Not stubbed, simply not exported.

Declared in cusparse.h but not exported by libcusparse.so (12.6.2, CUDA 13.0), which defines only the plain *_bufferSize of gebsr2gebsc. Calling one fails to link, so cusparse.cppm carries only the declaration (WWR_DECLARED_CHECK). Recorded in cusparse.json's declared_not_linkable.

Declared in cusparse.h but not exported by libcusparse.so (12.6.2, CUDA 13.0), which defines only the plain *_bufferSize of csr2gebsr. Calling one fails to link, so cusparse.cppm carries only the declaration (WWR_DECLARED_CHECK). Recorded in cusparse.json's declared_not_linkable.

Omitted from the neutral layer as part of the DEFERRED external memory / semaphore family below. Until ROCm 10.0.0 it was also not exported by libamdhip64 at all (declared-only, WWR_DECLARED_CHECK); the 10.0.0 pin DOES export it, so that second reason has lapsed and test/hip/hip_runtime_api.cppm carries both checks behind WWR_HIP_SINCE_7_15. See docs/architecture.md section 21.

The graphics-interop family (cudaGraphics* / hipGraphics*: OpenGL / Direct3D / EGL / VDPAU resource registration and mapping) is DEFERRED for v1, not rejected. wwr targets compute and no neutral graphics-interop layer is scoped; both backends declare the family, so this is a deliberate, reversible omission rather than an absent counterpart. Listed before the broad graph entry below because the cudaGraph* wildcard there also prefix-matches these names.

The CUDA execution-graph API -- Graph / GraphExec / GraphNode construction and update, stream-capture-to-graph, and the device-side graph-memory and child-graph-node helpers -- is DEFERRED for v1, not rejected. The few entry points the existing wrappers already use (wwrGraphCreate / GraphDestroy / GraphExecDestroy / GraphLaunch / GraphUpload / GraphInstantiate and the wwrGraph_t / wwrGraphExec_t handles) stay wrapped; the rest of the ~130-symbol surface is a deliberate, reversible omission until a neutral graph layer is scoped. The cudaGraph* wildcard also prefix-matches the graphics-interop names documented separately above.

The external memory / semaphore interop family (import, map, signal, wait and destroy of Vulkan / D3D / NvSci external resources and timeline semaphores) is DEFERRED for v1, not rejected: it has no neutral consumer and pulls in platform handle types wwr does not model. Deliberate, reversible omission. The single declared-not-linkable HIP member is documented separately above (externalmemorygetmappedmipmappedarray).

Present in the pinned ROCm 7.2.4 intersection but NOT reachable in the ROCm 7.1.0 floor build the CMakeLists enforces (hip-floor CI leg): hipStreamCopyAttributes / hipOccupancyAvailableDynamicSMemPerBlock are only declared inside the __HIP_DISABLE_CPP_FUNCTIONS__-guarded C++ helper region (which runtime_api.h suppresses), and hipLibraryEnumerateKernels is absent from the 7.1.0 hiprtc/library headers entirely. Wrapping any of them compiles at the pin and fails at the floor. Omitted until the ROCm floor rises; the raw single-vendor modules (which do not define that macro) still carry the first two.

A spurious name-collision, not a shared entity: cudaJitCacheMode is an ENUM CONSTANT of cudaJitOption on CUDA, while hipJitCacheMode is an ENUM TYPE on HIP. They normalise to the same key but are different kinds, so neither WWR_RT_VALUE nor WWR_RT_TYPE can bind both -- there is nothing to wrap. The genuinely shared jit names (JitCacheOption*, JitOption, etc.) are wrapped normally.

The thread-block CLUSTER family (scheduling policy, the cluster func/launch attributes, the two occupancy queries and the invalid-size error) became shared only when the pin moved to ROCm 10.0.0 -- CUDA 13.0 had it, the ROCm 7.1.0 FLOOR does not. Wrapping it is DEFERRED, not rejected, and the blocker is structural rather than per-name: src/detail/runtime_api_names.h carries 487 aliases and no version guard at all, because the neutral layer assumes every name it aliases exists on both backends at every supported version. A floor-gap guard convention has to be decided before any of these can be aliased. #334 has the design options.
